protocol: Chronological cases in all five real videos. Every model receives the exact same SHA256-verified frozen JPEGs and displayed timestamps through the production API, same guides and system prompt; selected reasoning effort recorded in metadata where supported. No expected answers/IDs passed to the model. Independent visual review is distinct from strict stage ID and lexical concept recall. Single observations do not establish sustained completion.

results.reference_answer: The oblique lifted-shoe example S2 is most consistent with the anchor: a free shoe is visibly raised behind the grounded supporting leg. A return to the floor should only be reported if it appears in the supplied sequence.

observation.summary: The latest view shows one brown shoe raised behind the supporting leg, with the other shoe visibly at the floor against a purple wall. The raised shoe is partly cropped at the upper edge; this matches the oblique lifted-shoe example.
observation.guidance: Follow the raised shoe until both shoes are clearly visible at the floor within this same shot. Do not count the blurred near-floor pass as a confirmed contact or completed return.
observation.principle: Use clear shoe–floor relationships within one uninterrupted shot; this reduces mistaken contact and repetition judgments without establishing technique safety.

phase_evidence.evidence: The close oblique view shows the free shoe raised behind the supporting leg while the supporting shoe remains at the floor, distinguishing this rearward lift from a forward extension.

observation.concern: Motion blur during the low pass and cropping of the latest raised shoe limit contact assessment; no clear physical hazard is visible.

results.question: Which visible guidance phase is shown here? Describe the visible evidence and any limits on declaring the phase complete.
results.reference_answer: Machine-tool activity is the phase: a mounted workpiece or tooling appears in the machine work area. Parameters and acceptance are unverified.

observation.summary: The latest view shows a projecting metal fixture plate with two rounded holders, dark rails, and cables inside a machine enclosure. The plate changes position and orientation across the recent frames, but a separate workpiece, cutting tool, and contact point are not clearly identifiable.
observation.guidance: Observe the next clear machine view for a distinguishable tool, mounted workpiece, and their relative motion. Record the visible fixture movement without treating it as proof of cutting or a completed machining cycle.
observation.principle: Separating visible machine movement from inferred machining reduces the risk of falsely recording process completion; montage shots do not establish one continuous production job.
observation.concern: No specific physical hazard is evident; shadow and the viewing angle limit identification of the working region.

observation.principle: Use ordered shoe positions within the same shot; this reduces mistaken contact and cycle judgments without establishing technique quality or safety.
